PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality wide-moat franchise navigating a genuine cost-pressure trough. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): YoY growth remains positive (revenue +7.4%, EPS +5.8% in Q3 FY2026), cash generation is healthy (OCF/NI ≈ 1.02x), and the balance sheet is investment-grade solid (ROE 29.7%). However, margins are compressing sequentially (gross margin 49.5% vs 51.0% YoY, operating margin 21.6% vs 23.1% YoY), driven by tariff headwinds (~$400M after-tax in FY2026) and surging oil costs (~$1B annualized after-tax if oil sustains near $100). Volume inflection of +2% in Q3 is encouraging but only one quarter. Three-year revenue CAGR of 2.3% lags peers. Pillar 2 (valuation): P/E of 22.96x is near the low end of its 365-day range (21.7x–26.7x), and P/B at 6.81x is also near the bottom of its range (6.4x–7.9x). However, the earnings yield of 4.4% now falls slightly below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.41%, eliminating the traditional premium PG commands over risk-free rates — so the multiple compression is partly justified by the rate environment, not purely a mispricing. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): Q3 results beat consensus (adjusted EPS $1.59 vs $1.56 est, revenue +3.5% beat) and the stock rose 3% on the print, but guidance was biased lower toward the low end of $6.83–$7.09 range. The 15% non-manufacturing headcount reduction (~7,000 jobs) is a structural cost improvement, but savings will take time to materialize. No clear near-term re-rating catalyst beyond hoping oil retreats. Net: a quality franchise at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation, but margin headwinds are real and partially uncontrollable, and the rate backdrop compresses justified multiples. Mildly attractive, not a conviction buy.
